plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since my value is $49 (the maximum possible value), I should bid my true value to maximize expected profit while eliminating risk of overpaying.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid my true value of $44, I win whenever the highest competing bid is below $44, and I pay whatever that second-highest bid is—never more than my value allows for profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $44 to maximize expected profit.
